content:
We need to list elements that can be definitively identified based on isotope distribution patterns visible in the mass spectrum. We need the mass spectrum data. Use mass_spectrometry_spectra tool. Then analyze isotopic patterns: look for characteristic isotopic spacing and relative intensities. For example: Chlorine (Cl) shows M+2 ~ 1/3 intensity of M (35Cl 75.8%, 37Cl 24.2% => M+2 about 1/3). Bromine (Br) shows M+2 ~ equal intensity (79Br 50.7%, 81Br 49.3%). Sulfur (S) shows M+2 ~ 4% (32S 95%, 34S 4.2%). Carbon shows M+1 ~ 1.1% per carbon (13C). Hydrogen shows M+1 ~ 0.015% (2H). Nitrogen shows M+1 ~ 0.37% (15N). Oxygen shows M+2 (18O) ~0.2% and M+1 (17O) ~0.04%. So we need to look at the spectrum to see peaks with characteristic spacing (e.g., 2 Da apart) and relative intensities.

Let's get the spectrum.
